sub_indicators.label: Digital links and facilities shared with other African countries
sub_indicators.subject: gov.regional
sub_indicators.text: Shared regional infrastructure: digital links and facilities shared with other African countries
sub_indicators.norm_short: The African Union's Programme for Infrastructure Development in Africa and its Digital Transformation Strategy ask states to join their networks across borders, give landlocked countries a route to the sea cables and share exchange points and data centres.
criteria: A source from the past three years says the country has no digital link with a neighbour, or stands outside the shared links of its region, and none is on record.

In the past three years the country has agreed to build or join a link or facility shared with another African country: a cross-border fibre link, a sea cable joining two African countries, a shared exchange point, data centre or satellite. Talks, a study or a bid to host do not count.
Building has started in the past three years: a contract awarded, works begun or cable being laid. A tender opened or money promised does not count.
A shared link or facility is in service: lit, commissioned or opened to traffic. A ceremony for the start of works, or a test, does not count.

It is reported carrying another country's traffic in the past three years: published figures of capacity sold or traffic carried across the border, a named user from the other country, or a fault that cut the other country's service.
